caseno: Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 97 of 2004
lawyer:
Md Khurshid Alam Khan Advocate instructed by ASM Khalequzzaman, Advocate-on-Record—For the Petitioner. 
Not Represented—The Respondents.
parties:
Razia Khatun ----- Petitioner 
Vs. 
Idris Ali and another ----- Respondents
full_judgment:
Md. Ruhul Amin J: This petition for leave to appeal has been filed against the judgment dated March 13, 2004 of the High Court Division in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 4255 of 2001 discharging the Rule. The Rule was issued upon an application filed under section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC) The said application under section 561A of the CrPC was filed against the judgment and order dated November 30, 2000 of the Court of Sessions Judge, Mymensingh in Criminal Appeal No. 23 of 2000 allowing the appeal upon setting aside the judgment and order dated April 30, 2000 of the Court of Magistrate, 1st Class, Mymensingh in CR Case No. 376(1) of 1995 convicting the respondent No. 1 under section 6(5) of the Muslim Family Laws Ordinance, 1961 and sentencing him to one year simple imprisonment. 

 2. The petitioner filed the aforementioned CR case alleging that during subsistence of the marriage between her and the respondent, the respondent has married for the 2nd time without the consent of the petitioner and that also without taking permission of the Arbitration Council. The Court of Magistrate held that the respondent married for the 2nd time without taking permission from the Arbitration Council and also without the consent of his first wife and thereupon convicted and sentenced the respondent as stated hereinabove. The respondent went on appeal before the Court of Session and the learned Sessions Judge allowed the appeal on the finding that the learned Magistrate on an erroneous view of the evidence on record convicted and sentenced the respondent. As against the judgment of the Court of Session the petitioner moved the High Court Division upon filing an application under section 561A of the CrPC and obtained the Rule. The petitioner in support of her moving the High Court Division by filing an application under section 561A of the CrPC against the judgment and order of the Court of Session asserted since she could not file appeal as per provision of section 417(2) of the CrPC within the time prescribed by section 417(3) of the CrPC and consequently she having had no other remedy filed the application under section 561A of the CrPC. 

 3. The High Court Division discharged the Rule on the finding "that the present application under section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure against an order of acquittal passed by the appellate Court is neither maintainable in the present forum nor the impugned judgment of acquittal calls for interference under the extraordinary jurisdiction on the ground canvassed before us. The High Court Division further observed that power under section 561A of the CrPC in the instant case would have been exercised by the High Court Division, had the order of conviction and sentence been passed absolutely without any legal evidence, but the order of acquittal has been passed because of absence of legal evidence as to the allegation. The High Court Division was also of the view that the petitioner ought to have moved the High Court Division under section 439 of the CrPC as against the order of the Court of Session. We are of the view that the observation made by the High Court Division is quite correct. Moreover, the ground i.e. time for filing an appeal under section 417(2) of the CrPC expired and, as such, the application under section 561A of the CrPC was filed not legally sustainable.
